blocks.text: AI Resources Data Stores in AI Security provides an inventory of the data stores associated with your AI environment, especially those connected to agents, MCP servers, models, and AI workloads. Use this view to understand what data sources your AI systems can access and to quickly spot configuration and security posture gaps.
The AI Resources - Data Stores Page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: View AI-related data stores in one place, with key metadata such as tags, account, subscription, or project, and scan status.
Quickly identify data stores with posture risks, e.g., not encrypted or logging not enabled using posture labels.
Understand where sensitive data may exist by viewing the top DLP engines triggered by a data store.
Use Open Graph to explore relationships between data stores and related AI resources (agents, models, workloads) for impact analysis and troubleshooting.
Track last scanned and scan status to confirm whether findings reflect the latest environment state.

blocks.heading: About the AI Resources - Data Stores Page

blocks.text: On the AI Resources Data Stores page (AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Data Stores), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Filter by Business Units.
View the following widgets for a quick, at-a-glance summary of your data stores:

Data Stores by Risk Level: Distribution of data stores by severity level among the data store’s open security issues. The severity level is categorized as Critical, High, Medium, Low, or Unknown. If the value is None, no open issues are currently detected.
Data Stores by Status: Distribution of the data stores by their governance status, e.g., Sanctioned (reviewed and approved), Unsanctioned (reviewed and not approved), or Unreviewed (awaiting review).

Sensitive Data Exposed to AI: Distribution of data stores that contain sensitive data, such as PII, PHI, PCI, and are connected to at least one AI model, agent, or workload. Because AI systems can access these data stores, the sensitive data could be unintentionally disclosed or leaked. You can also view the total count of files with sensitive-data matches across those data stores.
Search for specific data in the searchable columns.
Apply filters to view specific data.
View the list of data stores. For each data store, you can see:
Name: The name of the data store. Click the entity name to view additional details.
General Information: Information such as region, type, path, source, account ID, account name, and sensitive data. Click More Details for a graphical view.

Risk Level: Indicates the potential blast radius if this data store is compromised. The rating is based on capabilities such as system command execution, file write or delete access, credential storage or access, and outbound (external) network calls.
Lifecycle: Timeline showing the stages an AI agent goes through from discovery to deployment, monitoring, and updates, with timestamps for key milestones.
The detailed information page also displays the following tabs:
Graph View

The graph for an AI service is a visual representation of the data scan result for the service. It depicts the access path for the AI service (Azure AI Foundry Hub or AWS Bedrock Knowledge Base) where it has access to the storage account containing sensitive data. AI Security also detects if the AI service is publicly exposed to the internet, including the public exposure path, and the list of entities that can access the AI service. These details are helpful to quickly evaluate and remediate the issues, protect the sensitive data, and maintain a strong security posture.
Click the nodes to view additional details of each entity.
Data Security

Use this tab to view details of the sensitive record, including the DLP engines and dictionaries that match the record, the security posture of the record, ID and tags, and the timestamp of the last completed scan as follows:
Matched Files: The number of files that matched the DLP engines.
Triggers: Number of alerts raised for the resource.
DLP Engines: The DLP engines that match sensitive records.
DLP Dictionaries: The dictionaries associated with the DLP engines.
Document Categories: The category of document detected in the resource.
Document Types: The number of documents detected in the resource.
You can do the following in the data security table:
Search for a specific sensitive file.
Filter data by Linked Datastore, Sensitive DLP Engines, DLP Engines, DLP Dictionaries, Database, or Document Type.
View a list of sensitive files which were discovered. For each sensitive file you can view:
File Name
File Path
File Size
DLP Engines
DLP Dictionaries
Document Types
Last Completed Scan
Created Date
Issues
Use this tab to view a list of issues that were discovered. For each issue, you can view:
Issue ID: The unique identifier for the issue.
Policy Name: The policy title.
Policy Category: The threat category, e.g., public exposure, data loss, etc., that the policy belongs to.
Risk Level: The risk level, i.e., Critical, High, Medium, or Low.
Cloud Account: The unique identifier of the cloud account in which the model is located.
Created On: The date and time the issue was created.
Last Updated: The date and time the issue was last updated.
Type: Type of data store.
Environment: The cloud service provider in which the data store is present.
Risk Level: The risk level of the data store based on the risk score.
Status: Governance status of the data store.
Access Type: The permission level granted to the entity for the selected resource, e.g., Read, Edit, or Full Access.
Source: Name of the resource type.
Asset Risk: The security posture assigned to the data store (Dormant Identity, MFA Disabled, etc.). Hover over the label to see the description of each posture.
Last Completed Scan: Timestamp of when the last scan was completed.
